name: GS1 web resolver family (GS1 Digital Link URI, GS1-Conformant Resolver, RFC 9264 linksets, GS1 Web Vocabulary link types, GS1 data carriers)
scope_note: Covers the GS1 route from a physical data carrier to a passport document: the GS1 Digital Link URI syntax (release 1.7.0), the GS1-Conformant Resolver Standard (release 1.2.1) with its normative linkset schema, JSON-LD context and resolver description file schema, the GS1 Web Vocabulary link types (including gs1:dpp), the EPC Tag Data Standard 2.3 and the EPC binary compression standard 1.0.0 as the RFID path, GS1 in Europe and GS1 AISBL DPP papers (GS1-specific content only), open-source GS1 tools (Resolver CE, resolver test suite, syntax engine, toolkits, OpenEPCIS translator), the UNTP Identity Resolver as a GS1-compatible profile, the IANA 'dpp' link relation, and the Battery Pass technical guidance as a pilot reference. It leaves out: the content of any EN, ISO, IEC or DIN document (ISO/IEC 18975, 15459, 15418, 18004, 16022, 18000-63, 19987/19988, IEC 61406, the EN 182xx DPP standards) beyond bibliographic numbers; EPCIS event semantics (family m-event-traceability); verifiable-credential verification details (UNTP family); the GS1 General Specifications text (page too large to fetch); and any live resolver, including id.gs1.org, which was never contacted. Law articles are cited from the project's sibling records because EUR-Lex returned empty pages in this session.
summary: The GS1 web resolver family makes the identifier on the product a web address. A GS1 Digital Link URI carries a GS1 primary key (for a DPP usually GTIN, AI 01) and optional key qualifiers in a fixed path order (for GTIN: 22 consumer product variant, 10 batch/lot, 21 serial), behind any host name and an optional custom path stem; other GS1 Application Identifiers go in the query string. The URI is encoded in a QR Code or Data Matrix, or in RFID tag memory through EPC binary schemes that the EPC Tag Data Standard 2.3 can translate back to a Digital Link URI with a custom domain. A GS1-Conformant Resolver at that host answers HTTP requests for the URI. Without a link-type request it redirects to the single gs1:defaultLink of the identified entity; with linkType=<type> it redirects to that link or returns 404; with linkType=linkset or Accept: application/linkset+json it returns all links as an RFC 9264 linkset that must validate against the GS1 linkset schema. Links carry a link type from the GS1 Web Vocabulary, a title, and optional hreflang, media type and context attributes; links defined at a coarser level (GTIN) are inherited by finer levels (batch, serial). The vocabulary now has a stable link type gs1:dpp ('Digital Product Passport'), and IANA registers a plain 'dpp' relation whose reference is the UNTP Identity Resolver; UNTP tells clients to treat the two as the same. Every resolver publishes a description file at /.well-known/gs1resolver that names its root and supported primary keys. The GS1 resolver standard specifies 400 for a syntax error, 404 for an unknown entity or link type, 300 with a linkset for an unresolvable choice, never 200 for an error, CORS, GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, query-string pass-through, and tolerance of a trailing slash, but it names no redirect status code. The end-to-end flow is: scan carrier, read the URI, send it to the resolver (directly or through a pattern-based redirect such as gs1:handledBy), select the DPP link from the redirect or the linkset, then fetch and validate the passport, whose format the resolver does not define. GS1 papers present this as the single-carrier route to a DPP and argue that the parsed GS1 keys, not the domain, are the persistent identifier. For the engine, nearly every resolver behaviour is observable from outside by HTTP requests to a loopback fixture, but today's identifier.parse accepts only /01/<GTIN>/21/<serial>, the transport hides redirect hops and refuses OPTIONS without an authorization scope, and a linkset JSON object would pass identifier.resolve as if it were a passport.

maturity.spec_status: Ratified GS1 standards (voluntary industry specifications, not law). The GS1 Web Vocabulary is a ratified, versioned vocabulary (current 1.18.0). The UNTP Identity Resolver is a work-in-progress UN/CEFACT specification declared suitable for pre-production pilots. maturity.adoption_evidence: GS1 in Europe states that the GS1-Conformant Resolver standard has significant implementations by solution providers, brands and GS1 Member Organisations, and reports a global retail migration to 2D codes with GS1 Digital Link targeted for 2027 with readiness percentages per solution category (GS1's own claims, not independently verified). The Resolver CE README says at least three GS1 Member Organisations use version 3.0. The resolver standard cites a description file of the GS1 AISBL resolver at https://id.gs1.org/.well-known/gs1resolver (not fetched). Peer-reviewed prototypes: Made2Verify (GS1-compliant resolver with fallback dashboard, lab and production demonstration with a remanufacture part, Procedia Computer Science 277, 2026), a KAIST-led GS1-conformant resolver deployed for a port supply chain and DPPs (IEEE RFID-TA 2025), and the R-Cycle plastics DPP based on GS1 (Polymers 2024). The Battery Pass Technical Guidance (v1.0, March 2024) names GS1 Digital Link as one way to embed IDs in URLs but does not mandate it. No GS1 Digital Link or linkset use was found in the CIRPASS-2 GitHub code (code search, 0 hits); its most active repositories (pushed up to 2026-10-15) are ontologies and documentation.
maturity.regulatory_alignment: EU law does not name GS1 Digital Link, the GS1-Conformant Resolver or any link type. Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1) points (a)-(b) require a DPP to be connected through a data carrier to a persistent unique product identifier; Art. 10(1) point (c) ties the carrier and identifier to the standards of Annex III second paragraph or equivalents (Annex III names ISO/IEC 15459; bibliographic only); Art. 10(1) point (d) asks for open standards and an interoperable, machine-readable, transferable format without vendor lock-in; Art. 10(1) points (f)-(g) let the delegated act fix model, batch or item granularity; Art. 10(3) requires a digital copy of the carrier or identifier for dealers and online marketplaces; Art. 10(4) requires a back-up copy through a DPP service provider; Art. 13 creates the registry of unique identifiers and Art. 13(5) the unique registration identifier. Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/1736 publishes six harmonised DPP standards (content not read: protected). Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(3) makes the battery passport reachable through a QR code that links to a unique identifier, and Art. 77(10) adds upload of that identifier to the ESPR registry. GS1 maps model/batch/item to GTIN(+22) / GTIN+10 / GTIN+21 and argues that its keys meet the Annex III identifier standard; that is a GS1 claim (secondary for the protected standard). Article content here comes from sibling records espr.json and commission-2026-acts.json (retrieved 2026-10-13/15); EUR-Lex returned empty pages in this session.

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: Identifier = GS1 primary key plus key qualifiers expressed as a Digital Link URI path. Shape: <scheme>://<host>[/<customURIstem>]/<primaryKeyAI>/<value>[/<qualifierAI>/<value>...][?<AI>=<value>&...][#fragment]. Primary keys (URI Syntax 4.3): 01 GTIN, 8006 ITIP, 8013 GMN, 8010 CPID, 414 GLN, 415 Pay-To GLN, 417 Party GLN, 8017 GSRN provider, 8018 GSRN recipient, 255 GCN, 00 SSCC, 253 GDTI, 401 GINC, 402 GSIN, 8003 GRAI, 8004 GIAI. Qualifiers (4.4): 22 CPV, 10 batch/lot, 21 serial, 8011 CPID serial, 254 GLN extension, 8020 payment ref, 8019 SRIN, 235 TPX, 7040 UIC. Order for GTIN is 22 then 10 then 21; each qualifier is optional; 235 forms a separate GTIN+TPX path. GTIN must be 14 digits (shorter GTINs left-padded since 1.4.0). AI values use the 82-character set (XCHAR), CPID the 39-character set, AI 8030 the 64-character set; reserved characters are percent-encoded. Path is case sensitive after the host. Convenience alphas (gtin, lot, ser, cpv) were removed in 1.3.0. Query-string keys linkType and context are reserved for resolvers; extension keys must not be all-numeric. A canonical URI (4.12) uses https, host id.gs1.org, 14-digit GTIN, only AI keys in the query sorted lexically, no linkType/context, no trailing slash. Compressed URIs are recognised by RE2 (legacy) or RE3 (prefix 'eh' lowercase hex or 'ex' URI-safe base64 of an EPC binary string). GS1 granularity mapping for a DPP (GS1 in Europe paper): model = GTIN or GTIN+22, batch = GTIN+10, item = GTIN+21; identifiers are never reused once allocated.

L01_unique_identifiers.observable_black_box: The URI string read from the carrier or sample artifact: path segments, AI codes, GTIN check digit, qualifier order, character sets, percent-encoding, query keys, presence of a compressed segment. Equivalence of two URIs can be decided by parsing to AI key-value pairs and comparing those, independent of host.
L01_unique_identifiers.law_delta: Law requires a persistent unique product identifier at the granularity of the delegated act, compliant with Annex III standards or equivalents (Reg. (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1)); it does not require a URI form, a host, or GS1 keys. GS1 adds a web-resolvable syntax and the claim that the parsed keys, not the domain, are the persistent identifier.

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: Optical: QR Code or Data Matrix encoding the uncompressed GS1 Digital Link URI as plain text (GS1 Implementation Considerations, Method 1). GS1 in Europe calls QR Code with Digital Link 'highly likely' for its DPP AIDC application standard and notes Data Matrix as smaller and rectangular-capable but not natively read by consumer phone cameras. RFID (RAIN/UHF): EPC binary in the EPC bank per TDS 2.3; schemes SGTIN-96/198, SGTIN+ and DSGTIN+ (TDS 2.0) and twelve new '++' schemes (SGTIN++, DSGTIN++ and others, TDS 2.3) that add lossless binary encoding of a custom domain name so that a reader can rebuild a non-canonical Digital Link URI; the air interface is EPC UHF Gen2 (GS1 standard; ISO/IEC 18000-63 bibliographic only). The compression standard lets an EPC binary string ride in a URI as '<stem>/eh<hex>' or '<stem>/ex<base64url>'. NFC: can carry a Digital Link URI and is read natively by phones, but GS1 in Europe says NFC is not yet an approved GS1 carrier. GS1 states that any optical carrier can be copied, so the carrier itself cannot be authenticated. For retail packaging, GS1 guidance offers three point-of-sale 2D options: GS1 DataMatrix with an element string (no web link), QR Code with a Digital Link URI (opens with a phone camera), and Data Matrix with a Digital Link URI; during transition the 2D code sits next to the EAN/UPC, and scanners may convert a scanned URI to element string data for the till. The guidance recommends a brand-owned domain and short URIs because URI length drives symbol size.

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: HTTP/1.1+ over TLS (resolver CS-2, CS-3). Methods GET, HEAD, OPTIONS; CORS enabled (CS-4; no header values fixed; the test suite checks Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Methods containing GET, HEAD and OPTIONS). Default resolution: request without linkType redirects to the gs1:defaultLink target (CS-15) unless headers allow a better gs1:defaultLinkMulti match; no redirect status code is specified (Resolver CE uses 307). Specific link: ?linkType=<CURIE or URI> (for example gs1:dpp) redirects to that link (CS-17) or returns 404 (CS-18). Several equal candidates: 300 Multiple Choices with the linkset. Linkset: ?linkType=linkset or Accept: application/linkset+json returns 200 with the RFC 9264 JSON linkset, no redirect (CS-10); application/json is recommended to give the same; application/ld+json gives JSON-LD with context; text/html or no Accept gives an HTML page with the linkset embedded as JSON-LD. A linkset response should carry Link: <context URL>; rel="http://www.w3.org/ns/json-ld#context"; type="application/ld+json" (CS-13). Errors: 400 for a URI that fails syntax validation (CS-7), 404 for a valid URI with no data (CS-8), never 200 for an error (CS-9). Query string: all key=value pairs passed on when redirecting (CS-19; the option to drop them was removed in 1.2.0). Trailing slash tolerated (CS-25). Accept-Language should drive selection (CS-20); context query key may disambiguate. Compressed EPC URIs are decompressed (CS-5) and a redirect to another resolver uses the uncompressed URI (CS-6). Pattern-based redirection (2.8): a resolver may forward whole URI patterns (by GS1 Member Organisation or GS1 Company Prefix) with Location and optionally Link rel gs1:handledBy. Since 1.2.0 a Link header pointing to the linkset is no longer required on redirects, and since 1.0.0 dumping all links into the Link header is deprecated. UNTP IDR profile adds: linkset queries must be answered without authentication, resolvers that vary on Accept should send Vary: Accept, Accept-Language must not filter the linkset, linkType=all is a legacy alias clients should not send.

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.mechanism: The GS1 resolver standard defines only the read side (resolution and linkset retrieval). It defines no create, update, deactivate or search API. Implementations add their own: Resolver CE v3.0 exposes a separate bearer-token data-entry API (POST /new batch, PUT idempotent merge by (linktype, hreflang, context), partial DELETE with a JSON body, OpenAPI at the service root) storing linksets in MongoDB; GS1 Member Organisation resolvers expose their own portals (not examined). The passport API behind the DPP link is out of scope of GS1 resolver standards. The linkset itself is a machine-readable discovery document that GS1 in Europe says can be embedded in a web page so that crawlers can discover the DPP without a scan.

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.observable_black_box: Only the read side is observable without authorization: linkset content before and after an announced update, HTML pages with embedded JSON-LD linksets. Write APIs are vendor-specific and need an authorization scope.
L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.law_delta: Law requires DPP data to be searchable and transferable and creates a public web portal (Reg. (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1) point (d), Art. 14 per sibling record); GS1 provides discovery of links, not search over passport content.

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.mechanism: Linkset JSON (RFC 9264): {"linkset":[{"anchor":"<uncompressed DL URI>","description":"...","<relation>":[{"href":"...","title":"...","type":"<media type>","hreflang":["en"],"context":[...],"fwqs":true,"public":true}]}]}. GS1 schema (draft-07, URL https://ref.gs1.org/standards/resolver/linkset-schema): top-level only 'linkset'; entries require 'anchor', allow 'description' and deprecated 'itemDescription'; relation keys must match lowercase-hyphen tokens (IANA style, for example 'describedby') or full http(s) URIs made only of letters, digits, '.', '/' (the character class is written A-z, which also admits '[', '\\', ']', '^', '_', '`'); targets require href and title; hreflang items must be two letters or two letters-hyphen-two letters; additionalProperties false at every level. JSON-LD context (https://ref.gs1.org/standards/resolver/linkset-context, @protected) maps gs1 to http://gs1.org/voc/, linkset to @nest, anchor and href to @id, hreflang to dcterms:language, type to dcterms:format, title to dcterms:title. Link types come from the GS1 Web Vocabulary (60 link-type properties in v1.16, all subproperties of gs1:linkType); DPP-relevant: gs1:dpp, gs1:sustainabilityInfo, gs1:certificationInfo, gs1:instructions, gs1:serviceInfo, gs1:safetyInfo, gs1:traceability, gs1:epcis, gs1:masterData, gs1:jws, gs1:registryEntry, gs1:recallStatus, gs1:verificationService; resolver-only: gs1:defaultLink, gs1:defaultLinkMulti, gs1:handledBy; gs1:productSustainabilityInfo is deprecated. The vocabulary declares owl:equivalentProperty to https://gs1.org/voc/<term> and https://www.gs1.org/voc/<term> for most link types but not for gs1:dpp. IANA registers plain 'dpp' (reference UNTP IDR); UNTP uses https://test.uncefact.org/vocabulary/link-type/{dcc,dfr,dte,dia,dcr} for credentials. Resolver description file (/.well-known/gs1resolver) requires resolverRoot (uri) and supportedPrimaryKeys (enum all, 01, 8006, 8013, 8010, 410-415, 417, 8017, 8018, 255, 00, 253, 401, 402, 8003, 8004); optional name, supportedLinkType [{namespace, prefix}], linkTypeDefaultCanBeLinkset (default false), supportedContextValuesEnumerated, supportedContextValuesExternal, contact (vCard), extensionProfile, jsonLdContextLocation. The passport document behind the gs1:dpp link has no GS1-defined schema; it may be HTML, JSON-LD using GS1 Web Vocabulary terms, a UNTP DPP credential (application/vc+jwt per UNTP examples), an AAS, or a battery data model. The copy of the schema in the gs1/linkset repository, which the GS1 resolver test suite loads from gs1.github.io, is identical to the ref.gs1.org schema on every pattern and required array; a looser basic RFC 9264 schema in the same repository requires only href.

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: The resolver stores links, not passports. Persistence relies on (a) never reusing GS1 keys, (b) keeping the host in the carrier resolvable, and (c) re-pointing links without reprinting the carrier. GS1 papers note that a manufacturer domain in the URI may lapse, while the parsed keys stay registered independent of the domain; GS1 in Europe proposes that a client replace the domain with an alternative resolver, or that the EU registry act as lookup of last resort (listing primary and backup DPP URLs, possibly as DID service endpoints), and that federated GS1-conformant resolvers can redirect to backups. These are proposals, not specified behaviour. Made2Verify adds a fallback dashboard that keeps essential data when an OEM disappears. No GS1 link type for a backup copy exists in the vocabulary (v1.16 list read).

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: GS1 resolution is public by design: no authentication in the resolver standard. Access tiers are left to the target systems. The linkset schema has a boolean 'public' attribute (link can be shared publicly) with no normative processing rule found in the standard text read. context and Accept-Language select among links but are not access control. UNTP IDR requires public, unauthenticated linkset answers and defers extended (authenticated) linksets to a future version. Resolver CE secures only its data-entry API (bearer token, constant-time comparison) and limits Content-Type reflection to an allowlist.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.law_delta: Law requires access rights per delegated act and restricted parts (Reg. (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(1) points (f)-(g); Reg. (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77(9) implementing acts). GS1 resolver standards add nothing on access control.

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.mechanism: Transport integrity only (HTTPS). Linksets and redirects are not signed. The vocabulary offers gs1:jws (link to a JSON Web Signature) and gs1:verificationService (GS1 Lightweight Messaging Standard for product verification). GS1 states that optical carriers can be copied and cannot authenticate the product. UNTP requires clients to verify the dereferenced credential and says resolvability does not prove the subject stands behind the record. GS1 also publishes a VC data model repository and verifier (gs1/VC-Data-Model, gs1/vc-data-model-verifier; not examined).

L09_registry_and_customs.mechanism: No GS1 standard defines interaction with the EU registry. GS1 in Europe argues that the parsed keys (GTIN, lot, serial) rather than the URL should be uploaded to the registry, and asks whether non-government registries such as Verified by GS1 could support operator verification. gs1:registryEntry exists as a link type to a register entry. Registry and customs matching is therefore on parsed GS1 keys plus the Art. 13(5) unique registration identifier.

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.mechanism: Indirection is the update mechanism: the printed URI stays fixed while links in the resolver change. A new model-level identity needs a new GTIN (GTIN Management Rules, per GS1 in Europe). For repair or remanufacture, GS1 in Europe describes two options: the original DPP lapses, or the repairer issues a new DPP for the same serialised identifier that links to the original; it notes that brand owners may not link to third-party DPPs. GS1 standards define no versioning of links, no deactivation status and no end-of-life link type; TDS and EPCIS cover event history (other family).

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.law_delta: Law requires versioning, handover after re-use or remanufacture and an end of life for the battery passport (Reg. (EU) 2023/1542, Art. 77 per sibling record). GS1 resolver standards specify none of these.

L11_roles_and_governance.mechanism: GS1 AISBL and 100+ GS1 Member Organisations issue GS1 Company Prefixes; brand owners allocate GTINs and serials. Anyone may run a GS1-Conformant Resolver for URIs on their host; the standard stresses that each resolver is sovereign over its own URI space and need not give the same answers as another resolver. The GS1 AISBL resolver (id.gs1.org) serves the canonical host and can hand off by GS1 Company Prefix pattern to brand resolvers (gs1:handledBy). Standards are made under the GS1 Global Standards Management Process; implementation is under the GS1 IP Policy (royalty-free or RAND, per the vocabulary licence statement). Service providers sell resolver hosting. UNTP positions a resolver per scheme or per issuing register.

end_to_end_flows.name: Consumer scan to default page (no app)
steps: 1. Camera decodes the QR Code and reads https://id.brand.example/01/09506000164908/10/LOT1/21/SER1.
2. Browser sends GET with Accept: text/html.

3. Resolver validates syntax (400 on failure), looks up links for serial, batch and GTIN levels (walk-up union), and redirects to gs1:defaultLink (status not fixed by GS1; 307 in Resolver CE), passing any query string on.
4. Browser follows Location to the target page, which may or may not be the DPP (UNTP warns that GS1 retail defaults are usually consumer pages).
5. If the target is a landing page, it may embed the JSON-LD linkset that lists the gs1:dpp link.

end_to_end_flows.name: Machine client to DPP through linkset
steps: 1. Read and parse the Digital Link URI; normalise (14-digit GTIN, decompress if 'eh'/'ex').
2. GET the URI with Accept: application/linkset+json (or ?linkType=linkset).
3. Expect 200 and Content-Type application/linkset+json, with a Link header to the JSON-LD context.
4. Validate the linkset against the GS1 schema; find the anchor equal to the uncompressed URI.
5. Select the link whose relation is gs1:dpp (any namespace form) or IANA 'dpp'; check its type and hreflang.
6. GET the href; validate the passport (schema, context, signature) and check that its identifier matches the parsed GS1 keys.

end_to_end_flows.name: Direct DPP request by link type
steps: 1. GET <DL URI>?linkType=gs1:dpp.
2. Resolver redirects to the DPP link or answers 404 if no gs1:dpp link exists at any level.
3. Client follows the redirect and validates the passport.

end_to_end_flows.name: RFID tag to DPP
steps: 1. Reader inventories tags and reads the EPC bank (for example SGTIN++ with a custom domain name).
2. Middleware decodes the EPC binary with TDS 2.3 rules into GS1 element strings and a non-canonical Digital Link URI on the encoded domain (or a compressed 'eh'/'ex' URI on a known stem).
3. Client resolves the URI as in the machine flow; GS1 notes that phones cannot yet isolate one UHF tag, so this flow is mainly B2B.

end_to_end_flows.name: Compressed URI from NFC or RFID
steps: 1. Carrier yields <stem>/ex<base64url> or <stem>/eh<hex>.
2. Resolver (CS-5) treats the part before the compressed string as the URI stem, decodes 6 or 4 bits per character to the EPC binary, decodes the EPC per TDS, and builds the uncompressed path.
3. Resolver answers as for the uncompressed URI and uses the uncompressed URI as linkset anchor (CS-10) and in any onward redirect (CS-6).

end_to_end_flows.name: Delegation from GS1 global resolver to brand resolver
steps: 1. Client resolves https://id.gs1.org/01/<GTIN>/21/<serial>.
2. The global resolver matches the GS1 Company Prefix pattern and redirects the whole request unchanged to the brand resolver, with Location and optionally Link rel gs1:handledBy.
3. The brand resolver applies its own links.

end_to_end_flows.name: Failover after loss of the brand domain (GS1 in Europe proposal)
steps: 1. Resolution of the carrier host fails.
2. Client extracts the GS1 keys from the URI and substitutes another known resolver host, or queries the registry as lookup of last resort.
3. Client reaches the backup copy. This flow is not specified in any GS1 standard.

end_to_end_flows.name: Distance selling
steps: 1. The economic operator gives the seller the carrier URI (Reg. (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 10(3)).
2. The seller page links the same URI.
3. A click follows the consumer-scan flow.

failure_modes.fault: Accept header split on commas without trimming spaces or removing q-values, so 'text/html, application/linkset+json' gets a redirect instead of the linkset (seen in Resolver CE web_namespace.py).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Send Accept variants with spaces and q-values; expect 200 linkset each time.

failure_modes.fault: Query string appended to a target that already has one, producing a Location with two '?' characters (Resolver CE appends '?'+query unconditionally).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Configure a target with a query; request with a query; parse Location per RFC 3986 and compare parameters.

failure_modes.fault: Link header pointing to the linkset uses rel="application/linkset" (a media type) instead of the registered relation 'linkset' (Resolver CE).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Parse Link header; check relation tokens against the IANA registry.

failure_modes.fault: JSON-LD context Link header targets the namespace IRI http://www.w3.org/ns/json-ld#context instead of a context file, declares type text/html, and leaves a URI rel unquoted (Resolver CE).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Strict RFC 8288 parse of the Link header; fetch the target and check Content-Type application/ld+json.

failure_modes.fault: Soft error: unknown GTIN or invalid URI answered with 200 and an error page.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Crafted invalid and unknown URIs; expect 400 and 404.

failure_modes.fault: Requested link type missing, resolver falls back to the default link instead of 404.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Request ?linkType=gs1:dpp on an entity without a DPP link; expect 404.

failure_modes.fault: Permanent redirect (301/308) for the default link, so caches keep an outdated target after the link is re-pointed.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Record redirect status per hop; flag permanent codes as a risk finding (GS1 sets no code, so not a fail).

failure_modes.fault: Walk-up implemented as a redirect from /01/<GTIN>/21/<serial> to /01/<GTIN>, losing the serial for the target.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Observe first hop for an unknown serial; Location must not be a less granular Digital Link URI.

failure_modes.fault: Missing CORS headers on error responses or on OPTIONS preflight, breaking browser clients.
failure_modes.detectable_by: OPTIONS and GET on valid, invalid and unknown URIs; check Access-Control headers.

failure_modes.fault: Only legacy linkType=all supported; linkType=linkset and Accept-based linkset requests redirect.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare responses for linkType=all, linkType=linkset and Accept: application/linkset+json.

failure_modes.fault: Compressed 'eh'/'ex' URI not decompressed (400 or 404), or linkset anchor left in compressed form.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Request compressed equivalents of known URIs; compare with uncompressed responses and anchors.

failure_modes.fault: Trailing slash treated as a different resource (404).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare responses with and without a trailing slash.

failure_modes.fault: Linkset relation keys use http://gs1.org/voc/dpp while a client looks for https://ref.gs1.org/voc/dpp (or the reverse), so the DPP link is missed.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Engine normalises relation keys via a pinned equivalence table and reports the form used.

failure_modes.fault: Non-vocabulary GS1-prefixed link types (gs1:productPassport, gs1:repairInfo) used instead of gs1:dpp.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Check every gs1:-namespace relation against the pinned Web Vocabulary link-type list.

failure_modes.fault: Two gs1:defaultLink entries for one anchor, or a default carrying hreflang/context attributes.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Count defaults per anchor; check attributes.

failure_modes.fault: Valid BCP 47 hreflang such as 'zh-Hant' or 'es-419', or a hyphenated relation URI, rejected by the GS1 schema regex, so a correct resolver fails schema validation.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Report schema-pattern failures on these fields as a separate finding, not as a resolver fault.

failure_modes.fault: Resolver returns a linkset JSON object at the carrier URL and the engine treats it as the passport (false pass of identifier.resolve; identifier.consistency then compares against a missing id).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Classify the final body: top-level 'linkset' array means linkset.

failure_modes.fault: Description file uses linkTypeDefaultCanBeAll or omits resolverRoot; resolverRoot does not match the serving host.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Validate /.well-known/gs1resolver against the pinned schema; compare resolverRoot with the request origin.

failure_modes.fault: DPP link declares type application/ld+json but serves text/html (or no type).
failure_modes.detectable_by: HEAD/GET the href and compare Content-Type with the declared type.

failure_modes.fault: GTIN-13 in the path accepted silently and padded, or rejected, inconsistently across carrier, resolver and passport id.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Parse all three; apply the canonical-form rule; report the inconsistency.

failure_modes.fault: Qualifiers in the wrong order (/01/x/21/y/10/z) or serial with characters outside the 82-character set without percent-encoding.
failure_modes.detectable_by: identifier.parse against the pinned ABNF.

failure_modes.fault: Brand domain in the carrier lapses; no alternative resolution path exists.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Scheduled observation reports transport failure; check whether the ICS declares a backup or alternative resolver.

failure_modes.fault: QR and Data Matrix (or RFID) on the same product carry different key values.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Decode all carrier samples and compare parsed keys.

failure_modes.fault: Anonymous linkset lists URLs of restricted documents (for example links marked public=false).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Canary URLs in restricted links; scan the anonymous linkset and HTML landing page.

failure_modes.fault: Resolver answers the carrier URL with 200 and an application/linkset+json body, and the engine reports the identifier as resolved to a passport.

sources.license_or_reuse_terms: (c) 2025 GS1 AISBL with a linked disclaimer; no open licence stated
sources.what_it_shows: Characters 0-200000 of 393666 read through WebFetch. Compares three POS-capable 2D options: GS1 DataMatrix with element string, QR Code with GS1 Digital Link URI (readable by the default phone camera), and Data Matrix with Digital Link URI (needs an app). Says some scanners can turn a scanned Digital Link URI into element string data for the POS host; sets an Ambition 2027 transition target; gives placement and quiet-zone guidance; recommends a brand-owned domain and notes that shorter URIs give smaller symbols. No mention of DPP, compressed URIs, a URI length limit or a QR error-correction level was found in the part read. Its print-quality reference to an ISO/IEC verification standard was not followed (rule 5).

open_questions: Which redirect status code should the engine expect? The GS1 resolver standard names none; Resolver CE uses 307. Proposal: accept any 3xx except 300 as redirect, record the code, and flag 301/308 as a risk, pending an owner decision.

Which namespace form is the oracle for gs1 link types: https://ref.gs1.org/voc/ (standard text, vocabulary), http://gs1.org/voc/ (normative JSON-LD context), or https://gs1.org/voc/ (owl:equivalentProperty, Resolver CE)? gs1:dpp has no declared equivalents. The engine needs a pinned equivalence table approved by the owner.
